claim: Experience and changes in neuronal activity can alter CNS myelination.
source: Experience and changes in neuronal activity can alter CNS myelination, but the signalling pathways responsible remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general premise of the study.

claim: Endothelin signalling through endothelin receptor B and PKC epsilon regulates the number of myelin sheaths formed by individual oligodendrocytes in mouse and zebrafish.
source: Here we define a pathway in which endothelin, signalling through the G protein-coupled receptor endothelin receptor B and PKC epsilon, regulates the number of myelin sheaths formed by individual oligodendrocytes in mouse and zebrafish.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Social isolation in mice leads to reduced myelin sheath number in the prefrontal cortex.
source: We show that this phenotype is also observed in the prefrontal cortex of mice following social isolation
evidence: This is demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Social isolation is associated with reduced expression of vascular endothelin in the prefrontal cortex.
source: and is associated with reduced expression of vascular endothelin.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Increasing endothelin signalling rescues the myelination defect caused by social isolation.
source: Additionally, we show that increasing endothelin signalling rescues this myelination defect caused by social isolation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by intranasal administration of EDNRB agonist as shown in Figure 6.

claim: The vasculature responds to changes in neuronal activity associated with experience by regulating endothelin levels.
source: Together, these results indicate that the vasculature responds to changes in neuronal activity associated with experience by regulating endothelin levels, which in turn affect the myelinating capacity of oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: Social interactions, sensory stimulation and several forms of learning alter white matter and myelin structure in both humans and animal models.
source: For example, social interactions, sensory stimulation and several forms of learning have been shown to alter white matter and myelin structure in both humans and animal models (Scholz et al., 2009; Makinodan et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012; Sampaio-Baptista et al., 2013; McKenzie et al., 2014; Etxeberria et al., 2016; Xiao et al., 2016; Hughes et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Increasing the level of neuronal activity by using optogenetics or chemogenetics enhances the generation of myelin-forming oligodendrocytes and increases the amount of myelin they form.
source: At the level of individual neurons and axons, increasing the level of activity by using optogenetics or chemogenetics enhances the generation of myelin-forming oligodendrocytes and increases the amount of myelin they form (Gibson et al., 2014; Mitew et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Preventing synaptic vesicular release from axons reduces myelin formation.
source: whilst preventing synaptic vesicular release from axons reduces myelin formation (Hines et al., 2015; Mensch et al., 2015; Koudelka et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: EDN expression by endothelial cells increases with enhanced blood flow.
source: First, EDN expression by endothelial cells increases with enhanced blood flow (Yanagisawa et al., 1988; Dancu et al., 2004; Walshe et al., 2005; Pandit et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The EDN G-protein coupled receptor endothelin receptor B enhances myelination in slice cultures.
source: Second, the EDN G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR) endothelin receptor B (EDNRB) enhances myelination in slice cultures (Yuen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: EDN is expressed by CNS vascular cells.
source: Here we show that EDN is expressed by CNS vascular cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: EDN expression lessens in the medial prefrontal cortex following social isolation.
source: and that this expression lessens in the medial prefrontal cortex following social isolation
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Social isolation leads to impaired cortical myelination.
source: which we confirm also leads to impaired cortical myelination.
evidence: This is demonstrated by oligodendrocyte morphology analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Reduced EDN signalling decreases the number of myelin sheaths formed by individual oligodendrocytes in vivo.
source: Correspondingly, we show, by manipulating EDNRB signalling in rodent and zebrafish models, that reduced EDN signalling decreases the number of myelin sheaths formed by individual oligodendrocytes in vivo.
evidence: This is demonstrated by conditional knockout experiments in mice (Figure 3) and zebrafish mutant analysis (Figure 5).

claim: Intranasal administration of an EDNRB agonist rescues the reduction in myelination associated with environmental social deprivation.
source: Finally, we rescue the reduction in myelination associated with environmental social deprivation by intranasal administration of an EDNRB agonist to activate EDN signalling within the CNS.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Social isolation in mice during a critical period comprising 2 weeks after weaning reduces the excitability of specific subtypes of pyramidal neurons of the medial prefrontal cortex.
source: Prior work has established that social isolation in mice during a critical period comprising 2 weeks after weaning reduces both the excitability of specific subtypes of pyramidal neurons of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and oligodendrocyte formation and myelination in the same area (Liu et al., 2012; Makinodan et al., 2012; Yamamuro et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Social isolation in mice during a critical period comprising 2 weeks after weaning reduces oligodendrocyte formation and myelination in the medial prefrontal cortex.
source: Prior work has established that social isolation in mice during a critical period comprising 2 weeks after weaning reduces both the excitability of specific subtypes of pyramidal neurons of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and oligodendrocyte formation and myelination in the same area (Liu et al., 2012; Makinodan et al., 2012; Yamamuro et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Isolated mice spent significantly less time than socially-experienced controls interacting with a novel mouse.
source: We repeated this protocol, confirming the previously-described effect on circuit function by showing that isolated mice spent significantly less time than socially-experienced controls interacting with a novel mouse (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Individual oligodendrocytes in socially isolated mice made fewer myelin sheaths in the medial prefrontal cortex.
source: Using this approach we showed that individual oligodendrocytes made fewer myelin sheaths (Figure 1F–H)
evidence: This is demonstrated by CNPase immunostaining and morphological analysis shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: The length of the myelin sheaths formed by oligodendrocytes in socially isolated mice was unaffected.
source: although the length of the myelin sheaths formed by oligodendrocytes in these mice was unaffected (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by morphological analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F.

claim: Isolated mice generated fewer oligodendrocytes in the mPFC.
source: Further, we found that the isolated mice also generated fewer oligodendrocytes in the mPFC (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell counting data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D.

claim: Social isolation had no effect on myelin sheath number in the visual cortex.
source: In contrast, social isolation had no effect on myelin sheath number in the visual cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B), demonstrating the region-dependent effects of this protocol on myelination.
evidence: This is demonstrated by morphological analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: Edn1 and Edn3 mRNA are robustly expressed in laminin-positive blood vessels in control mice.
source: We confirmed robust Edn1 and Edn3 mRNA expression in controls, localised to laminin-positive blood vessels, which co-expressed the endothelial/pericyte marker Pecam1 mRNA (Figure 2A) (Yanagisawa et al., 1988; Hammond et al., 2014).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2A and supported by citations.

claim: Edn1 expression has been observed in astrocytes following demyelination.
source: While previous studies have observed Edn1 expression also localised to astrocytes following demyelination (Hammond et al., 2014) and microglia (Zhang et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: No Edn1, Edn2 or Edn3 mRNA was observed in S100β positive astrocytes or IBA1 positive microglia in the healthy mouse brain.
source: here we observed no Edn1, Edn2 or Edn3 mRNA in S100β positive astrocytes or IBA1 positive microglia (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B), indicating that endothelial cells and/or pericytes are the main source of Edn in the healthy mouse brain.
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Endothelial cells and/or pericytes are the main source of Edn in the healthy mouse brain.
source: indicating that endothelial cells and/or pericytes are the main source of Edn in the healthy mouse brain.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Edn is expressed in Pecam1-positive vascular cells but not in astrocytes or microglia.

claim: Following social isolation, the number of endothelial cells expressing Edn1 and Edn3 mRNA was significantly reduced in the mPFC.
source: Following social isolation, both the number of endothelial cells expressing Edn1 and Edn3 mRNA and the expression level of Edn1 mRNA within each cell was significantly reduced in the mPFC (Figure 2B–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization quantification shown in Figure 2B–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–G.

claim: Following social isolation, the expression level of Edn1 mRNA within each endothelial cell was significantly reduced in the mPFC.
source: Following social isolation, both the number of endothelial cells expressing Edn1 and Edn3 mRNA and the expression level of Edn1 mRNA within each cell was significantly reduced in the mPFC (Figure 2B–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization quantification shown in Figure 2B–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–G.

claim: The vascular area was unaffected by social isolation in the mPFC.
source: However, the vascular area and the number of cells expressing Pecam1 mRNA were unaffected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantification shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E.

claim: The number of cells expressing Pecam1 mRNA was unaffected by social isolation in the mPFC.
source: However, the vascular area and the number of cells expressing Pecam1 mRNA were unaffected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantification shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E.

claim: There was no effect of social isolation on Edn1 expression by Pecam1 cells in the visual cortex.
source: In contrast to the mPFC, there was no effect of social isolation on Edn1 expression by Pecam1 cells in the visual cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantification shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Loss of EDNRB in the oligodendrocyte lineage had no significant effect on oligodendrocyte progenitor cell or oligodendrocyte generation in the mPFC.
source: Comparison of the number of oligodendrocyte lineage cells in the mPFC in the control (Pdgfra-cre;Ednrbwt/wt) mice shown in Figure 1 with EDNRB cKO (Pdgfra-cre;Ednrbflox/flox) mice revealed no significant difference in the oligodendrocyte progenitor cell (OPC) or oligodendrocyte generation (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell counting data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Loss of EDNRB in the oligodendroglial lineage significantly reduced the number of myelin sheaths generated by individual oligodendrocytes.
source: However, loss of EDNRB in the oligodendroglial lineage significantly reduced the number of myelin sheaths generated by individual oligodendrocytes (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by morphological analysis shown in Figure 3B–D.

claim: EDNRB cKO oligodendrocytes demonstrated a 22% reduction in myelin sheath number compared to wild type littermates.
source: EDNRB cKO oligodendrocytes demonstrated a 22% reduction in myelin sheath number compared to wild type littermates, but the lengths of the remaining sheaths were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by morphological analysis shown in Figure 3B–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: The lengths of myelin sheaths were unchanged in EDNRB cKO oligodendrocytes compared to wild type littermates.
source: EDNRB cKO oligodendrocytes demonstrated a 22% reduction in myelin sheath number compared to wild type littermates, but the lengths of the remaining sheaths were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by morphological analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: A similar effect of EDNRB loss on myelin sheath number was seen in the visual cortex.
source: A similar effect of EDNRB loss on myelin sheath number was also seen in the visual cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by morphological analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: The effect of deleting EDNRB on myelin sheath number was identical to the myelination deficits of individual oligodendrocytes within the mPFC following social isolation in wild-type animals.
source: These experiments show that oligodendroglial EDNRB regulates the number of myelin sheaths formed by individual oligodendrocytes and, strikingly, that this effect of deleting EDNRB was identical to the myelination deficits of individual oligodendrocytes within the mPFC following social isolation in wild-type animals.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the phenotypes shown in Figure 1 and Figure 3.

claim: Cell type specific loss of EDNRB from the oligodendrocyte lineage caused a significant reduction in the amount of time that cKO mice spent with the novel mouse in the social interaction task.
source: Surprisingly, despite the additional effects of social isolation on oligodendrocyte number, the cell type specific loss of EDNRB from the oligodendrocyte lineage was sufficient to cause a significant reduction in the amount of time that cKO mice spent with the novel mouse in the social interaction task, although, as might have been expected, the effect size was smaller than in socially isolated mice, with a 33% reduction following social isolation and 20% following EDNRB cKO as compared to wild type mice (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The effect size on social interaction time was smaller in EDNRB cKO mice (20% reduction) than in socially isolated mice (33% reduction) compared to wild type mice.
source: although, as might have been expected, the effect size was smaller than in socially isolated mice, with a 33% reduction following social isolation and 20% following EDNRB cKO as compared to wild type mice (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing behavioral data from Figure 1C and Figure 3E.

claim: Loss of EDNRB signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells phenocopies a specific component of the response of oligodendrocytes to social isolation.
source: We conclude that loss of EDNRB signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells phenocopies a specific component of the response of oligodendrocytes to social isolation and that this, in turn, contributes to the behavioural deficits that result from social isolation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the phenotypes of EDNRB cKO and social isolation.

claim: Loss of EDNRB signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells contributes to the behavioural deficits that result from social isolation.
source: We conclude that loss of EDNRB signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells phenocopies a specific component of the response of oligodendrocytes to social isolation and that this, in turn, contributes to the behavioural deficits that result from social isolation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that EDNRB cKO mice show reduced social interaction similar to isolated mice.

claim: Treatment with the EDNRB agonist BQ3020 significantly increased the number of myelin sheaths produced by individual rat oligodendrocytes in microfiber cultures.
source: We saw a significant increase in the number of myelin sheaths produced by individual oligodendrocytes 11 days later in response to the EDNRB agonist (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by microfiber culture experiments shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: BQ3020 increased myelin sheath number in wild type mouse oligodendrocytes but had no effect on EDNRB cKO oligodendrocytes in microfiber cultures.
source: Similar results were obtained with wild type mouse oligodendrocytes (Pdgfra-cre;Ednrbwt/wt) while BQ3020 had no effect on EDNRB cKO (Pdgfra-cre;Ednrbflox/flox) oligodendrocytes (Figure 4F–G), confirming the specificity of the agonist for EDNRB.
evidence: This is demonstrated by microfiber culture experiments shown in Figure 4F–G.

claim: Treatment with the EDNRB antagonist BQ788 had no effect on myelin sheath number in microfiber cultures.
source: In contrast to the agonist, treatment with the EDNRB antagonist had no effect on myelin sheath number in these cultures (Figure 4A–C), as might be expected given the lack of EDN-expressing blood vessel cells
evidence: This is demonstrated by microfiber culture experiments shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: Neither EDNRB agonist nor antagonist altered myelin sheath length in microfiber cultures.
source: and neither agonist nor antagonist altered sheath length (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by microfiber culture experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: BQ3020 selectively activates EDNRB-mediated signalling pathways in oligodendrocytes that increase myelin sheath number in vitro.
source: We conclude from these experiments that the BQ3020 agonist selectively activates EDNRB-mediated signalling pathways in oligodendrocytes that increase myelin sheath number in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microfiber culture experiments.

claim: EDNRB activation increased the phosphorylation of serine-729 of PKC epsilon.
source: As shown in supplementary file 1, one of the largest changes in protein phosphorylation following EDNRB activation was an increase in the phosphorylation of serine-729 of PKC epsilon, an isozyme of the Protein Kinase C (PKC) family.
evidence: This is demonstrated by phospho-protein antibody array data.

claim: FR 236924, a specific activator of PKCε, promoted phosphorylation of PKCε at serine-729.
source: First, we examined myelination in oligodendrocyte microfiber cultures treated with FR 236924, a specific activator of PKCε, which promoted phosphorylation of PKCε at serine-729 (Figure 5A)
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot shown in Figure 5A.

claim: FR 236924 significantly increased myelin sheath formation in microfiber cultures.
source: and significantly increased myelin sheath formation (Figure 5B–C), similarly to BQ3020.
evidence: This is demonstrated by microfiber culture experiments shown in Figure 5B–C.

claim: The average number of myelin sheaths formed per oligodendrocyte was reduced by 31% in rse homozygous zebrafish (EDNRB Hom) compared to wild type controls.
source: Analysis of individual oligodendrocytes enabled by sparse labelling of these cells in the fish larvae revealed the same phenotype as in the EDNRB cKO mice; the average number of myelin sheaths formed per oligodendrocyte was reduced by 31% in rse homozygous fish (EDNRB Hom) compared to wild type controls (Figure 5F–G, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is demonstrated by zebrafish oligodendrocyte analysis shown in Figure 5F–G and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Myelin sheath length was unaffected in rse homozygous zebrafish compared to wild type controls.
source: while sheath length was unaffected (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by zebrafish oligodendrocyte analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–C.

claim: Activation of PKCε by FR 236924 treatment rescued myelin sheath number in rse homozygous zebrafish.
source: As predicted, activation of PKCε by FR 236924 treatment from 3 to 4 days post fertilisation, rescued myelin sheath number in rse homozygous fish (Figure 5D–G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by zebrafish experiments shown in Figure 5D–G.

claim: PKCε acts downstream of EDNRB in the regulation of myelin sheath number in vivo.
source: This result confirms a role for PKCε downstream of EDNRB in the regulation of myelin sheath number in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the zebrafish rescue experiments.

claim: 10 days of BQ3020 treatment to socially-isolated animals rescued the myelination phenotype normally seen in these mice.
source: Strikingly, and in keeping with our prediction, 10 days of BQ3020 treatment to socially-isolated animals rescued the myelination phenotype normally seen in these mice, with a 20% increase in the number of myelin sheaths formed by mPFC oligodendrocytes in treated animals, meaning that the sheath numbers were now not significantly different to wild-type animals housed in groups (Figure 6D–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by intranasal administration experiments shown in Figure 6D–E.

claim: Daily handling involved in the intranasal administration protocol did not negate the effects of social isolation on myelin sheath numbers.
source: Importantly, we confirmed that the daily handling involved in this protocol did not negate the effects of social isolation by showing that the sheath numbers in the control isolated mice administered saline had the same reduction in sheath numbers as completely isolated animals (Figure 6B and D–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing data from Figure 1 and Figure 6.

claim: EDN has contrasting effects on oligodendrocyte formation and on myelination.
source: The conclusion that EDN has contrasting effects on oligodendrocyte formation and on myelination highlights that these two steps in oligodendrocyte development are regulated independently.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that EDNRB affects myelin sheath number but not oligodendrocyte number in the healthy CNS.

claim: Oligodendrocyte formation and myelination are two steps in oligodendrocyte development that are regulated independently.
source: The conclusion that EDN has contrasting effects on oligodendrocyte formation and on myelination highlights that these two steps in oligodendrocyte development are regulated independently.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of EDN signaling on these processes.

claim: Astrocytic EDN hinders oligodendrocyte differentiation during remyelination.
source: Our findings on the role of EDN in myelination complement other investigations demonstrating a role of astrocytic EDN hindering oligodendrocyte differentiation during remyelination (Hammond et al., 2014; Hammond et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Global EDNRB mutant zebrafish have an increased number of oligodendrocytes.
source: In agreement with this observation, our global EDNRB mutant zebrafish were found to have an increased number of oligodendrocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by zebrafish oligodendrocyte counting shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: EDN signalling plays two roles: indirectly inhibiting oligodendrocyte formation, but promoting myelin sheath formation once differentiation has occurred.
source: Together previous studies and ours suggest that EDN signalling plays two roles, indirectly inhibiting oligodendrocyte formation, but, promoting myelin sheath formation once differentiation has occurred.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from integrating current findings with prior literature.

claim: Conditional loss of EDNRB from adult oligodendrocyte progenitors 3 days prior to demyelination had no effect on the percentage of remyelinated axons 14 days after injury.
source: At apparent odds with this conclusion, conditional loss of EDNRB from oligodendrocyte progenitors had no effect on remyelination; having deleted OPC EDNRB from adult mice 3 days prior to demyelination of the external capsule, Hammond and colleagues observed that the percentage of remyelinated axons, assessed by electron microscopy, was unchanged 14 days after injury (Hammond et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Myelin sheath numbers in cortical oligodendrocytes remain largely stable throughout life.
source: Based on recent live imaging studies showing that myelin sheath numbers in cortical oligodendrocytes remain largely stable throughout life (Hill et al., 2018; Hughes et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Endothelin-mediated regulation of sheath number is likely to occur around the birth of each newly formed oligodendrocyte.
source: we propose that any endothelin-mediated regulation of sheath number is likely to occur around the birth of each newly formed oligodendrocyte.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on prior imaging studies showing stable sheath numbers.

claim: Oligodendrocytes are continuously generated in the adult CNS.
source: The continuous generation of oligodendrocytes in the adult CNS, itself increased by activity-related signals ensures that dynamic regulation of endothelin signalling from the vasculature has the capacity to play a role in adaptive myelination throughout life.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about adult oligodendrogenesis.

claim: Cortical oligodendroglia show higher levels of expression of EDNRB than spinal cord oligodendroglia.
source: An intriguing possibility suggested by a comparison of gene expression in cortical oligodendroglia and spinal cord oligodendroglia showing higher levels of expression of EDNRB in the former (Horiuchi et al., 2017; Marques et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior gene expression studies.

claim: Cortical oligodendrocytes may be specialised for linking metabolic demand to support.
source: is that these cortical oligodendrocytes are specialised for this role linking metabolic demand to support.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on differential EDNRB expression.

claim: Oligodendrocytes in white matter might be more specialised for rapid axonal conduction.
source: By contrast, oligodendrocytes in white matter might be more specialised for rapid axonal conduction.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to contrast with cortical oligodendrocytes.

claim: Myelin provides metabolic substrates to the underlying axon via specific transporters within the inner layer of the sheath.
source: A key function of myelin is the provision of metabolic substrates to the underlying axon via specific transporters within the inner layer of the sheath (Fünfschilling et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012b; Meyer et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: NMDA receptor activation in oligodendrocytes following glutamate release by active axons relays the need for metabolic support of axons to oligodendrocytes.
source: Prior work has implicated that NMDA receptor activation in oligodendrocytes following glutamate release by active axons in relaying the need for metabolic support of axons to oligodendrocytes (Saab et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: An increase in EDN production by endothelial cells is predicted to occur in the presence of increased blood flow or hypoxia.
source: We now propose that an increase in EDN production by endothelial cells, as predicted to occur in the presence of increased blood flow or hypoxia, will increase myelin sheath generation by local oligodendrocytes and so provide a further means of linking energy supply and demand.
evidence: This is based on prior knowledge about EDN regulation by blood flow.

claim: Changes in blood flow and hypoxaemia are associated with increased cortical activity.
source: Changes in blood flow and hypoxaemia are associated with increased cortical activity (forming the basis of the BOLD signal detected by fMRI).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about neurovascular coupling and fMRI.

claim: An EDN-mediated pathway driving an increase in myelination is a plausible mechanism for ensuring that the metabolic demands of active axons are met.
source: Therefore, an EDN-mediated pathway driving an increase in myelination is a plausible mechanism for ensuring that the metabolic demands of active axons are met.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: Neuropathological studies of MS lesions reveal pre-myelinating oligodendrocytes unable to complete remyelination.
source: Neuropathological studies of MS lesions revealing pre-myelinating oligodendrocytes unable to complete remyelination suggest for that failure of this final step may contribute to pathology.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from MS neuropathology.

claim: Pre-existing adult oligodendrocytes contribute to repair in MS.
source: These findings emphasise that the already differentiated oligodendrocyte represents a possible target for remyelination strategies in MS, a conclusion reinforced by recent papers using Carbon14 dating, electron microscopy or snRNA seq of post mortem human MS material providing evidence that pre-existing adult oligodendrocytes contribute to repair (Duncan et al., 2018; Jäkel et al., 2019; Yeung et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: The already differentiated oligodendrocyte represents a possible target for remyelination strategies in MS.
source: These findings emphasise that the already differentiated oligodendrocyte represents a possible target for remyelination strategies in MS
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from neuropathological observations and recent studies.

claim: Increased levels of LIF secreted by cultured astrocytes in the presence of neuronal activity enhances myelination in vitro.
source: Such indirect signalling has been implied by in vitro studies, wherein increased levels of LIF secreted by cultured astrocytes in the presence of neuronal activity enhances myelination (Ishibashi et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells use blood vessels as a scaffold to migrate along during development.
source: For example, during development, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells use blood vessels as a scaffold to migrate along (Tsai et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Local oxygen levels influence oligodendrocyte differentiation, stalling the process when levels are low.
source: Once in place, local oxygen levels influence their differentiation into oligodendrocytes, stalling the process when levels are low. Only when an adequate oxygen supply is established are the cells able to differentiate and begin the process of myelination (Yuen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Axons in the cortex are discontinuously and sparsely myelinated.
source: Another way in which additional myelin sheaths might impact circuit function is the addition of sheaths to axons in the cortex that are discontinuously and sparsely myelinated (Tomassy et al., 2014; Hill et al., 2018; Hughes et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.
